articles.title: Pep Guardiola's Stance on USMNT Job After Mauricio Pochettino Exit Reportedly Revealed
articles.summary: United States men's national team fans hoping Pep Guardiola will be the next head coach reportedly might not want to get their hopes up at this point.
articles.body:
United States men's national team fans hoping Pep Guardiola will be the next head coach reportedly might not want to get their hopes up at this point.

Jason Burt of the Telegraph reported Sunday that "Guardiola will resist any attempts by the United States to hire him as their head coach" in large part because he wants to take a year away from the sport after leaving his role with Manchester City.

The United States position is open with Mauricio Pochettino departing for Manchester United.

Despite the apparent lack of immediate interest, Burt reported Guardiola remains "open" to at least meeting with the United States after previously living in the country after leaving Barcelona in 2012 prior to joining Bayern Munich.

That is notable since Burt pointed out "it is well known that Guardiola would, at some point during his career, like to manage a national team at a major tournament."

He turned down the Italy job in the past and, according to Burt, would also be interested in coaching either Brazil or England.

As for the Americans, ESPN's Jeff Carlisle reported United States women's national team coach Emma Hayes is among the group that will lead the search to find the next men's head coach. She will be joined by USSF CEO JT Batson, COO Dan Helfrich and VP of Sporting Oguchi Onyewu.

There is some momentum on the men's side of things after emerging from the group stage and reaching the round of 16 in the 2026 World Cup. It was the second straight World Cup the program reached the round of 16 after also doing so in 2022.

The Americans did not qualify for the 2018 World Cup but also reached the round of 16 in 2010 and 2014.

Guardiola is the type of high-profile coach who could potentially help the Red, White and Blue get over the hump and challenge for deeper runs in the World Cup and other international tournaments.

After all, he won 20 major trophies in his 10 seasons with Man City and set the Premier League points record with 100 during the 2017-18 campaign. The club became the first to win the Premier League four years in a row and also became the only English team to hold the Premier League title, FA Cup, Champions League title, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup at the same time.

Yet it seems like the Americans will have to turn elsewhere in their coaching search.

articles.title: Scotland: Louis van Gaal influence still with Sebastien Pocogonoli
articles.summary: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli says he draws on the influence of iconic manager Louis van Gaal in his own coaching career.
articles.body:
Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli says he draws on the influence of iconic manager Louis van Gaal in his own coaching career.

The Belgian worked under the legendary Dutchman during their time at AZ Alkmaar, a special period for Pocognoli during which he won the Eredivisie title in 2009.

Van Gaal also previously took charge of the Netherlands, and now that he has moved into international football himself, the Scotland boss reflected on the 75-year-old's influence.

"I take a lot from all of my gaffers, but probably he was the one with the most experience," Pocognoli told BBC Scotland.

"I was very young and you know in that moment he had all the Barcelona young players between his hands, also Ajax players.

"The way that he treats the young players in a direct way, honest way and hard way was for me really inspiring in my daily job now.

"I was lucky to have a lot of good coaches but he was probably the most that impressed me day by day, and I felt progress under him.

"That I think is the best thing for players as a feeling."

'Everything takes time if you want to build'

Progress is exactly what every Scotland fan is yearning for. Under Steve Clarke, the amount of that very commodity plateaued.

Years in the international wilderness were expelled with two European Championships and a World Cup appearance, but they were punctuated by disappointing results and dour tactics.

Pocognoli's arrival signified not only a new era, but a new approach, formation, selection and outlook.

It has been far from straightforward for the Belgian as he approaches 100 days in charge next week. Five games, two wins over North Macedonia, a draw in Slovenia and two humbling defeats mark his tenure so far.

Within it, a fresh system and injection of different faces to offer a break from the norm, but also plenty signs that a transformation will not be an immediate reality.

Scotland's failings in front of goal has remained, while it is clear the Scots are still getting to grips with a back three, albeit with enforced changes in personnel.

"Everything in life takes time to build if you want to achieve something," said Pocognoli.

You are Scotland boss Pocognoli - what would you do?

Six goals to go - will McGinn catch Dalglish & Law?

"So we know that in the performance world everything goes faster and quicker, but we have an objective and we know that we have to go through the up and down and the good moments. At the end I hope that all this experience can make us stronger.

"I don't ask the players to be patient, it's just to believe in what we are doing."

Pocognoli acknowledges he's not had much opportunity to immerse himself in Scottish culture after taking his first foray into international management.

A wander around Glasgow is about all he's managed. And any further exploring will have to wait until after Monday's Nations League test in St Gallen.

Finishing in the top two of their group seems a tall order for Scotland, who are requiring a win and snookers in Slovenia. It seems progression to the next Euros will instead roll on to the qualifying campaign next year.

"We don't have the control of what will happen because Slovenia will decide," Pocognoli said. "But if we want to have a chance to go through to the group stage and to go to the play-offs we have to go with the bravery and try to play with courage and try to force something.

"I don't believe that we are waiting for something then it will happen, so let's go through our quality and try to be aggressive and wait what happens in Slovenia."

articles.title: Ronaldinho makes comeback for Ravenna
articles.summary: Brazil legend Ronaldinho makes his comeback aged 46 for Ravenna, playing the first half of their Italian third-tier derby against Forli.
articles.body:
Brazil legend Ronaldinho made his comeback aged 46 for Ravenna in their 2-0 win over Forli in an Italian third-tier derby.

The 46-year-old came out of retirement for the Serie C club he joined as an investor in August, having last played in 2015 for Fluminense.

He started Sunday's game and showed some bright touches, and he was involved in the opening goal.

The former Barcelona superstar held off a defender before playing the pass that came before the assist for Giulio Donati's drive from outside the box.

He had earlier set up a chance for Donati from a corner, with the defender having his header saved.

At half-time there was a media circus around Ronaldinho, with journalists surrounding him, and former Brazil and AC Milan team-mate Dida joined him on the pitch.

Ronaldinho was substituted at the break with the score at 1-0.

A temporary stand, named the R10 in reference to Ronaldinho and his familiar shirt number, was built for the sold-out fixture at the Stadio Bruno Benelli.

The game was streamed in several countries around the world.

Ronaldinho trained once with the team, on Saturday, before Sunday's debut.

A team graphic beforehand showed him on the left side, but he mostly played centrally.

In his peak playing years, Ronaldinho was one of the best players in the world - as well as one of the most popular for his joyful demeanour and exuberant skill.

He won the 2002 World Cup with Brazil, the 2006 Champions League with Barcelona, and league titles with Barca and AC Milan - plus the Ballon d'Or and Fifa World Player of the Year awards in 2005.

He also played for Paris St-Germain as well as Gremio, Flamengo, Atletico Mineiro and Fluminense in his homeland, plus Mexican side Queretaro.

Ronaldinho scored 299 goals in his regular career and had been hoping to have a chance for number 300 for Ravenna. He would have taken a penalty had they been awarded one.

"It was lovely to be here, playing, having the build-up in the dressing room," Ronaldinho told Sky Sport Italia.

And asked if he might play again for Ravenna, who are second in their Serie C group, he said: "If the president calls me, I'll be back."

articles.title: Haaland no tiembla por la sanción al City: "Firmé un contrato de nueve años y medio"
articles.standfirst: Erling respondió a las especulaciones que lo sitúan fuera del conjunto 'cityzen'
articles.summary: Erling respondió a las especulaciones que lo sitúan fuera del conjunto 'cityzen'
articles.body: El Manchester City sigue a la espera de recibir una sanción que apunta a ser histórica por infringir las normas financieras de la Premier League entre las temporadas 2009-10 y 2017-18. Erling Haaland, sin embargo, se muestra tranquilo al respecto. No tiene nada que temer y reivindicó su fidelidad al conjunto 'mancuniano'. "¿2009? Creo que por aquel entonces jugaba en el Bryne. Lo hice hasta 2013. ¿Deberíamos continuar?", bromeaba en la previa del partido contra Gales, en el que volvió a ver portería desde el punto de penalti y, además, repartió una asistencia en favor de Schjelderup. "Es una buena pregunta a la que me cuesta responder", ya apuntó en tono más serio. "Es un caso entre la Premier League y el Manchester City, que se llevará ante un panel. Es un caso un poco difícil de responder cuando en realidad no sé mucho. No sé cuándo será la respuesta; no he leído mucho al respecto, para ser honesto", aseguraba un Erling Haaland que, para nada, se mostró preocupado. "Estoy concentrado en tratar de rendir para el Manchester City, un club con el que firmé un contrato de cinco años en 2022, y un contrato de nueve años y medio a finales de 2024", recalcó el ariete noruego. "Creo que eso es todo al respecto. Soy jugador del City, y estoy increíblemente feliz". Haaland, de este modo, cortó de raíz con las especulaciones que le sitúan fuera del Manchester City en función de la sanción aplicada. Tal y como adelantó 'Financial Times', se debería conocer el veredicto entre diciembre de 2026 y enero 2027. En su momento, de hecho, se llegó a rumorear que, en su última extensión de contrato, podría haberse incluido una clausula de salida.

articles.title: Scotland U21s: Eseosa Sule strikes late in draw with USA
articles.summary: St Mirren forward Eseosa Sule came off the bench to score a late penalty as Scotland U21s drew 1-1 with USA U23s in Spain.
articles.body:
Eseosa Sule came off the bench to score a late penalty as Scotland Under-21s wrapped up their Spanish training camp with a 1-1 draw against the United States Under-23 side in Murcia.

St Mirren striker Sule slotted home with six minutes remaining after Sam Chambers was upended in the box by Andre Gitau.

That cancelled out Frankie Westfield's early opener, the Philadelphia Union full-back firing a smart finish across Rory Mahady to give the Americans a 14th minute lead.

The result at the Pinatar Arena capped an excellent week's work for Tony Docherty's young Scots, following their emphatic 4-0 win over Ukraine on Thursday.

Manchester United midfielder Tyler Fletcher captained a strong Scottish side that also featured Udinese's Lennon Miller, Kyle Ure of Crewe Alexandra, and Hearts' forward James Wilson.

articles.title: Italian children's football tournament abandoned because of parents' fighting, spitting and abuse
articles.summary: A football tournament for nine and 10-year-olds in Italy is suspended because of parents fighting, spitting and shouting homophobic abuse at a child and a referee.
articles.body:
A football tournament for nine and 10 year olds in Bergamo, Italy, was abandoned because of the behaviour of parents, which included fighting and shouting homophobic insults towards a child and a referee.

The tournament was arranged by Serie D club Villa Valle, and Italian news agency Ansa reported , external that the referees used were young people involved at the club.

Organisers of the event and the coaches of all teams involved agreed to suspend the tournament during the final match of the day because of the parents' quarrels which also included spitting and booing opposing teams.

It also said that some children left the pitch crying.

Villa Valle posted a statement on social media, condemning the behaviour which they described as "painful to witness", but also praised the attitudes of the children playing and their coaches.

"Villa Valle wishes to express its strongest condemnation of the disrespectful and violent behaviour displayed by some parents in the stands," the club said.

"With deep disappointment, our club found itself compelled to take a decision that was as difficult as it was necessary: to bring the final match of the tournament to an early end and to suspend the awards ceremony, in order to send a strong and unequivocal message against attitudes that have nothing whatsoever to do with the values of sport.

"After a day characterised by matches played in a spirit of fairness, mutual respect and sportsmanship by the young athletes and coaching staff, it was particularly painful to witness such deplorable incidents in the stands.

"We strongly believe in the educational value of sport, especially at youth level, and we are convinced that adults should serve as positive role models for young people, not become the protagonists of behaviour that risks undermining the true meaning of these events."

articles.title: Aberdeen: Mario Frick is new head coach at Pittodrie
articles.summary: Former Liechtenstein striker Mario Frick is announced as the new head coach of Aberdeen.
articles.body:
Mario Frick has been announced as the new head coach of Aberdeen, taking over from the sacked Stephen Robinson to become the club's fourth manager in 2026.

Capped 125 times as a striker for Liechtenstein, the 52-year-old was last in charge at Luzern, leaving the Swiss club in the summer after five years.

He follows Robinson, Peter Leven and Jimmy Thelin in leading the side in this calendar year and will take charge for the first time against Scottish Premiership bottom side Kilmarnock on Saturday.

"Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team," said Pittodrie chief executive Adrian Bevington.

"He was also exceptionally well regarded by the many people across the game we consulted during the process, and the board was unanimous in its belief that he is the right person to lead Aberdeen forward."

Former Motherwell and St Mirren boss Robinson was dismissed on 9 November, with Aberdeen second bottom of the table and having lost four games in a row in all competitions.

'Aberdeen hunt yet another manager after ill-fated Robinson reign'

Latest Aberdeen news, analysis and fan views

Reputation for developing youngsters - and goal against Scotland

Frick, who also managed Vaduz in the Swiss Super League, will be assisted by Roman Matter and is the seventh permanent manager since Dave Cormack took control of the club in November 2019.

As a player, his former clubs include FC Basel, FC Zurich, St. Gallen and Grasshopper, while his 16 international goals make him Liechtenstein's all-time top scorer.

"Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play," added sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel. "He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

"We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I'm convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact."

Frick got Vaduz promoted in 2020 before helping Luzern avoid relegation following his move there in 2021.

The next again year he guided them to a fourth-placed finish and European qualification, although they were knocked out of Conference League qualifying by Lee Johnson's Hibernian.

Aberdeen say Frick "has built a strong reputation for transforming teams, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players during his coaching career".

Hibs striker Thibault Klidje and current Aberdeen goalkeeper Marius Muller both played under him.

Aberdeen did not disclose contract details for Frick as he takes over a side with just three wins from 12 Premiership outings this season.

One of his international goals came at Hampden Park in 2010 when a late Stephen McManus header rescued a 2-1 win for Scotland.

Ian: Left field but it is a bold decision. Let us get back up we we belong.

Kev: Could be good. Could be bad. If it is the latter the the Dons will be in real trouble. It's a very quick appointment...

Malky: A curve ball if ever there was one. I admit I was unaware of him; I had to Google him. As far as I'm aware he has a 37% win ratio, so he'll fit right into the current state this club finds itself in. I hope to be proved wrong, but for me it's underwhelming.

Harry: He certainly can't be any worse than the last few that have come and gone. Surely gonna hit the jackpot at some point.

articles.title: Arsenal 1-1 London City Lionesses: Gunners remain winless at home in the WSL after inspired Mary Earps denies them victory
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Arsenal's wait for a home WSL win goes on after a 1-1 draw against London City Lionesses; the Gunners have now drawn all five games at the Emirates this season; Frida Maanum's early strike was immediately cancelled out by Izzy Goodwin
articles.body:
While the result extends Arsenal's unbeaten home run to 24 league matches, it is becoming an increasing concern and a spectre on the shoulder that the Gunners have been unable to secure three points at the Emirates this year.

Giving her view to Sky Sports after the game, Renee Slegers - managing her 50th Arsenal game - said: "We spent more time than we normally do without the ball; partly the game plan and partly them asking questions of us on the pitch.

"We create big chances, could have done more with those. That's the frustrating part. This is the fifth [home game] and we couldn't give the fans the win. Unfortunately we couldn't do it for them."

It was two early goals that decided the fixture too. Frida Maanum scored for a second game in a row - having netted against Barcelona in the Champions League in midweek - slotting home from an Alessia Russo cross to put Arsenal ahead.

But a minute later, London City were level. Leah Williamson lost the run of the lively Izzy Goodwin, and the striker lashed into the roof of the net.

From then on, it was a goalkeeping masterclass from former England No 1 Earps especially that kept Arsenal from scoring another with her counterpart Misa Rodriguez also making her fair share of saves, albeit not as frequently.

The Gunners simply could not find a way past the inspired London City stopper as Lionesses boss Sarina Wiegman watched on from the stands.

The pick of her string of world-class saves came when she tipped a Maanum shot onto the crossbar. It came shortly after substitute Delphine Cascarino had also rattled the woodwork at the other end.

The result does little to improve either side's WSL standings, and Arsenal's hopes of finishing in the Champions League places takes another hit. They are sixth on 14 points - already six behind London City in third.

"We were happy with the one point, we wanted and needed three today," Slegers added. "Every game is three points for Arsenal when we play for this club.

"At the moment, with our position in the table and how we need to stay connected and compete for the top three positions for the Champions League, this one was very important for us.

"With that being said, the season isn't over. It's still November and we have to look at what it looks like in May."

10: GOAL! A sweeping move is finished by Maanum after Russo's cutback to give Arsenal the lead.

11: GOAL! London City immediately equalise as Goodwin fires into the roof of the net.

22: SAVE! Earps makes a good stop to deny Lisa Baum, who cuts in from the right-hand side.

27: SAVE! Misa Rodriguez on hand this time to deny Alexia Putellas.

29: SAVE! Again from Earps! This time it's a flying effort to keep out another Baum shot.

68: CROSSBAR! Cascarino pings an effort off the top of the woodwork.

77: DOUBLE SAVE! Earps pulls off another brilliant double save, first to deny Smith then Maanum.

85: CROSSBAR! Earps fingertips a Maanum shot onto the crossbar.

How's your luck? Arsenal face dazzling Earps as home woes continues

Analysis from Sky Sports' Charlotte Marsh at the Emirates:

Before Sunday's game, S ky Sports asked whether Arsenal have lost their fear factor at the Emirates this season.

The answer surely has to be yes - although after the game, Slegers was adamant that the fear factor has not gone, despite being without a win.

Teams have come to the Emirates and sat in a low block that the Gunners have been unable to break down more than once.

London City were never going to do that. It's not in their DNA. They closer resemble the Barcelona team Arsenal faced on Thursday where, funnily enough, they drew 1-1.

But what they might not have been banking on was an ingenious performance from Earps. While Arsenal did not have to worry about defenders sitting back, they did face a goalkeeper putting in one of the performances of the season. How's your luck?

She made eight saves as Arsenal continued to pepper her goal - her most in the WSL since 2017 - and the second-most in the WSL this season after the goalkeeper that replaces her at Man Utd, Phallon Tullis-Joyce.

When asked how she found the game, Earps told Sky Sports: "Tiring. It's a big point away from home.

"Either team could have won it in terms of chances. Happy with the point - would have liked three. All the girls put their bodies on the line. I love defending. It was tough today and I thought we did a good job."

It was perhaps made all the sweeter for her that her former England boss Sarina Wiegman was watching on. It is well-documented how she departed the national team, but it certainly showed the Lionesses head coach what she was missing.

Earps has had to bide her time at London City, with Elene Lete continuing to be the No 1 until recently. The former England No 1 has now started in three games, and while she is yet to keep a clean sheet, she will have staked a huge claim to the permeant spot with her performance on Sunday.

"Mary is amazing," her boss Eder Maestre said after the game. "It's not just because of the talent she has, she delivers the commitment and the togetherness that she can bring to the team because of her experience. Watching her in that performance was a pleasure."

Slegers: Players left everything on the pitch

Arsenal boss Renee Slegers to Sky Sports:

" Two good teams going against each other. I think we started the game well, score a very good goal, but we let them come back into the game too easily.

"I must say the players left everything on the pitch. They were absolutely dedicated, playing with hunger and focus. There are things in our game we must do better. We want to be dominating the ball. Being more ruthless. It's very basic but that's what it's about."

On Maanum: "She was very big for us against Barcelona and good for us tonight again. You can always count on her with runs into the box. The finish was very good."

On 50th Arsenal game: "I'm proud to represent Arsenal. I want to do everything I can for Arsenal."

Maestre: Our targets are bigger than a draw with Arsenal

London City Lionesses boss Eder Maestre to Sky Sports:

"We are happy because this kind of environment is always difficult to cope with, but at the same time, we want to win every game so we cannot be [too happy] just because it's the first time we've drawn against Arsenal.

"Our targets are even bigger. We have the hop to have the performance. We improve quite well in the second half. We had the chances, and they did as well.

"They're one of the best teams in the world and playing knowing that they need the points to push for the Champions League positions. We already knew how close it was going to be."

articles.title: Deion Sanders Hot-Seat Buzz Addressed by CFB Insider After Colorado's Massive Win vs. Houston
articles.summary: Colorado Buffaloes head coach Deion Sanders has faced mounting speculation about his job security, but the fourth-year coach "isn't going down without a fight," The Athletic's Stewart Mandel wrote on Sunday.
articles.body:
Colorado Buffaloes head coach Deion Sanders has faced mounting speculation about his job security, but the fourth-year coach "isn't going down without a fight," The Athletic's Stewart Mandel wrote on Sunday.

Sanders alleviated some of the concerns about his job with a stunning 42–32 upset over No. 14 Houston on Friday night.

It was Colorado's first victory against a top-15-ranked team since 2007. The Buffaloes offense erupted with explosive plays, scoring three 30-plus-yard rushing touchdowns and a 53-yard passing touchdown in just the second and third quarters. The victory improved Colorado to 4-6 with a 2-5 conference record.

There has been growing chatter about Sanders' job over the past two seasons. Colorado finished with a 9-4 record in 2024, which was Sanders' second season with the team. Heisman Trophy winner Travis Hunter and quarterback Shedeur Sanders departed for the 2025 NFL Draft, and the Buffaloes took a significant step backwards. Colorado finished with a 3-9 record last season.

Despite opening the 2026 season with two victories, the Buffaloes lost their next five games and appeared to be on pace to finish with the worst record in the Big 12. After losing nine consecutive Big 12 contests, Sanders has led Colorado to victories in two of the team's last three conference games.

Sanders signed a contract extension after the 2024 season, and Colorado would owe him a $25.5 million buyout if he were fired after this season, per CBS Sports . Colorado only guaranteed 75 percent of the coach's contract through 2029, but it would still be expensive to move on. Colorado professor Roger Pielke Jr. estimated it would cost the school $21 million more to fire Sanders than to keep him.

articles.title: Los hermanos Dos Santos reaparecen 'irreconocibles'
articles.standfirst: Giovani y Jonathan, excanteranos del Barcelona, se juntaron para jugar al pádel junto a Eder, su otro hermano
articles.summary: Giovani y Jonathan, excanteranos del Barcelona, se juntaron para jugar al pádel junto a Eder, su otro hermano
articles.body: Durante años compartieron vestuario, celebraciones y partidos con la Selección Mexicana, pero ahora Giovani y Jonathan dos Santos volvieron a reunirse lejos de las canchas de futbol. Los hermanos, que construyeron buena parte de sus carreras entre Europa, Estados Unidos y México, protagonizaron un nuevo encuentro deportivo, aunque esta vez dejaron de lado los tachones y el balón para disfrutar de una partida de pádel. Giovani y Jonathan dos Santos atraviesan una etapa diferente en sus vidas. Giovani permanece alejado del futbol profesional desde 2021, mientras que Jonathan cerró su ciclo con el América en junio de 2026, después de conquistar seis títulos con las Águilas, incluido el histórico tricampeonato de Liga MX. Ahora, los hermanos vuelven a compartir su pasión por el deporte con una actividad distinta, el pádel, mientras desarrollan sus proyectos personales fuera de las canchas. La historia de los hermanos Dos Santos sumó un nuevo capítulo con su reunión para practicar pádel, una disciplina que ha ganado popularidad entre futbolistas y exjugadores. Ambos jugaron junto a su hermano Eder, otro de los Dos Santos. Para Giovani, este deporte no es desconocido. Desde 2025 comenzaron a circular imágenes del exfutbolista participando en partidos y torneos, mostrando que continúa activo físicamente. Su presencia en las canchas de pádel también llamó la atención porque sus apariciones públicas se volvieron menos frecuentes después de su salida del América. Ahora, compartir esta actividad con Jonathan representa un nuevo acercamiento deportivo entre dos hermanos acostumbrados a competir juntos. Antes de reencontrarse en el pádel, Giovani y Jonathan dos Santos compartieron experiencias importantes dentro del futbol profesional. Ambos se formaron en las categorías inferiores del FC Barcelona, aunque sus trayectorias tomaron caminos diferentes. Posteriormente coincidieron en el Villarreal de España y en LA Galaxy de la MLS, además de representar a la Selección Mexicana. Los momentos que marcaron su historia: FC Barcelona: formación futbolística de ambos hermanos. Villarreal: coincidieron durante la temporada 2014-2015. LA Galaxy: volvieron a compartir vestidor en Estados Unidos. Selección Mexicana: representaron juntos al futbol nacional. Su trayectoria compartida convirtió a los Dos Santos en una de las parejas de hermanos más reconocidas del futbol mexicano. Después de su última etapa profesional con el América en 2021, Giovani dos Santos comenzó a desarrollar actividades empresariales. Jonathan, por su parte, ha combinado su trayectoria como exfutbolista del América con intereses personales fuera de las canchas. El encuentro demuestra que, aunque sus carreras siguieron caminos diferentes, ambos conservan una conexión con el deporte. Esta vez no hubo goles ni una camiseta compartida. Giovani y Jonathan dos Santos cambiaron el futbol por el pádel, pero mantuvieron intacta una de las historias familiares más conocidas del balompié mexicano.

articles.title: El ‘9’ de De Miguel, en el once de España: emotivo homenaje en el Metropolitano
articles.standfirst: Varios de los titulares posaron con camisetas de los distintos clubes del delantero fallecido, y Torres, Llorente y Casillas depositaron dos ramos de flores en el círculo central antes de un minuto de silencio
articles.summary: Varios de los titulares posaron con camisetas de los distintos clubes del delantero fallecido, y Torres, Llorente y Casillas depositaron dos ramos de flores en el círculo central antes de un minuto de silencio
articles.body: El Riyadh Air Metropolitano se sumó este domingo al duelo del fútbol español. Antes del arranque del España-Inglaterra de la Liga de Naciones, la selección rindió homenaje a Jesús de Miguel, el delantero del CD Tenerife tristemente fallecido el pasado 3 de noviembre a los 30 años, con un acto tan sobrio como emotivo. Los once titulares de España saltaron al césped para la foto previa sosteniendo, varios de ellos, una camiseta de uno de los clubes por los que pasó el futbolista a lo largo de su carrera. Sobre el verde se vieron las elásticas del Tenerife, de Unionistas de Salamanca, del Castellón, del Navalcarnero, del Internacional de Madrid y de los primeros equipos de su etapa de base, casi todas con el dorsal ‘9’ y el apellido “De Miguel” a la espalda. Un repaso visual a la trayectoria de un delantero hecho a sí mismo, especialista en ascensos, que había recorrido media geografía del fútbol modesto español antes de encontrar su sitio en Canarias. El gesto más solemne llegó a continuación. Tres leyendas del fútbol español —Fernando Torres, Fernando Llorente e Iker Casillas— portaron dos ramos de flores hasta el círculo central y los depositaron sobre el césped. Después, el estadio guardó un minuto de silencio que se respetó de principio a fin, sin un solo sonido que lo quebrara. De Miguel, madrileño de 1996, había construido su carrera a base de esfuerzo y goles en Segunda B, Primera RFEF y, finalmente, Segunda División. Delantero de 1,89 metros, combativo y temible en el juego aéreo, dejó mujer e hija. El fútbol español le ha despedido estos días con una ola de homenajes bajo el lema “Siempre en nuestro recuerdo”, que la selección quiso hacer suya en su última cita del año en casa.

articles.title: Women's Super League: London City's 'bravery' paying off in top three pursuit
articles.summary: After 10 games in the Women's Super League season, London City Lionesses have shown they are capable of finishing inside the top three.
articles.body:
After 10 games in the Women's Super League season, London City Lionesses have shown they are capable of finishing inside the top three.

Their narrow 2-1 defeat by Manchester City two weeks ago provided snippets of their potential but a 1-1 draw at the Emirates against an improved Arsenal on Sunday confirmed their credentials.

Eder Maestre's side sit third in the table - the last qualification spot for next season's Women's Champions League - and are six points above Arsenal.

It is a strong position to be in just shy of the halfway stage having already faced big hitters Arsenal, Manchester City and Manchester United.

Current leaders Chelsea await in December but, for now, London City's progress is moving at a pace that looks set to challenge the usual suspects.

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

A sold-out away end helped fill out the 32,000-strong crowd at the Emirates on Sunday as many hoped for an end-to-end encounter.

They were not disappointed as fearless London City showed bravery against an Arsenal side who played with a spark following their 1-1 draw with Barcelona.

The visitors were helped out by Arsenal's wastefulness - the Gunners had 17 shots and only converted one - but London City caused plenty of problems of their own.

Maestre said after their defeat by Manchester City that their opponents showed more experience and know-how but against Arsenal, his side matured.

They were under pressure early on and fell a goal down thanks to Frida Maanum's opener but it took just 98 seconds for Izzy Goodwin to equalise for London City.

That killed Arsenal's momentum and when the pressure increased again from the hosts in the second half, goalkeeper and player of the match Mary Earps stepped up to make crucial saves.

"The performance was there. We had the chances to score and get a better result but Arsenal had chances too. The game was very open," said Maestre.

"The way we faced and challenged every circumstance in the game shows we are here, and able to play with that mentality in these big games.

"We came here to take risks. Our energy was good. We were brave and weren't scared about the context or the opponent.

"We tried to play as if we were at home. I always want to feel that my teams are brave and go for the win."

That bravery showed as Alexia Putellas came close twice with long-range efforts, Goodwin could have been onside when she was played in behind later on.

London City hit the crossbar through substitute Delphine Cascarino and had 14 shots compared to Arsenal's 17, including four inside the box.

Arsenal are still yet to win at home this season in the WSL but this was still an impressive showing from London City, who came to the Emirates to play.

But while they were willing to take risks, they were smarter than they were against Manchester City, choosing when to press aggressively and when to hold off.

"We tried to match the pace of the ball and not expose ourselves as much to the players that Arsenal have," added Maestre.

"We were trying to mix the moments we were more clinical in our press. We made some adjustments at half-time and were much better at recognising those."

London City are backed by US billionaire Michele Kang and that has made a big difference in the transfer market.

They recruited superstars Alexia Putellas, Mary Earps, Mapi Leon and Kadidiatou Diani in the summer.

Such is their depth that high-flying Spaniard Lucia Corrales, the dangerous Cascarino and England international Freya Godfrey came off the bench.

Those individual talents have made a difference and on Sunday it was goalkeeper Earps who took the plaudits, claiming the player of the match award.

She made crucial saves late on as Arsenal pushed ferociously for a winner, tipping Maanum's effort onto the crossbar and blocking her shot from close range.

Earps had to bide her time for the number one shirt after making the switch from Paris St-Germain this summer but has started the past three WSL games.

"Mary is a very strong character and is much more than the things we see in terms of the performance," said Maestre.

"She has experience, and energy that you can bring to every part in the process and not just the things we see in the matches.

"I think the energy that she brings to the position is massive and has a massive impact. I'm very pleased with her."

Watching on in the stands was England boss Sarina Wiegman who will have been pleased with the display from goalscorer Goodwin.

The 23-year-old got the better of England captain Leah Williamson when she fooled her with quick feet and fired the ball into the back of the net, making it 1-1.

She is proof that competition for places in the London City starting XI is pushing players on and that their depth is improving each week.

"I think Izzy is becoming a more mature player. She has the inner competition and the signings sometimes push you to bring 100% every time," added Maestre.

"She is committed to keep pushing and, with the performances she is having, why not [earn an England call-up]?

"Izzy is moving forward in the ways she can take advantage and that commitment is the way she is reaching those performances. I'm very proud of her."

articles.title: El Dépor estalla con el arbitraje ante el Barça femenino: "Resulta inadmisible y compromete las garantías competitivas"
articles.standfirst: El equipo azulgrana empató en el 102' después de que el árbitro decidiera ampliar 8 minutos
articles.summary: El equipo azulgrana empató en el 102' después de que el árbitro decidiera ampliar 8 minutos
articles.body: El Deportivo ha expresado su "profunda indignación y disconformidad" con la actuación arbitral del encuentro entre el Dépor ABANCA y el Barcelona, disputado este domingo y que acabó con 1-1 tras el gol azulgrana en el minuto 102 de partido. El club gallego, a través de un comunicado oficial, centra su denuncia en la gestión del tiempo añadido, a su juicio incomprensible. Según explica el Deportivo en un comunicado, con el marcador de 1-0 el equipo arbitral señaló ocho minutos de prolongación e informó de que comenzarían a contabilizarse a partir del minuto 92. De acuerdo con esa indicación, el club sostiene que el encuentro debía haber terminado en el 100. Sin embargo, se extendió hasta el 107 y el gol del empate del Barcelona llegó en el 102. La entidad gallega califica esa gestión de "incomprensible e injustificable" y denuncia que no hubo una justificación objetiva que explicase la ampliación del tiempo anunciado. "El RC Deportivo quiere expresar públicamente su profunda indignación y disconformidad con la actuación arbitral registrada en el partido disputado este domingo, 15 de noviembre, entre el Dépor ABANCA y el FC Barcelona, correspondiente a la jornada 11 de Liga F, especialmente por la incomprensible gestión del tiempo añadido, que tuvo una incidencia directa en el desarrollo y el resultado final del encuentro. Con el marcador de 1-0, el equipo arbitral señaló ocho minutos de tiempo añadido en la segunda parte e informó de que estos comenzarían a contabilizarse a partir del minuto 92. En consecuencia, el encuentro debía finalizar en el minuto 100. Sin embargo, de manera incomprensible e injustificable, el partido se prolongó hasta el minuto 107, llegando el gol del empate del FC Barcelona en el minuto 102, cuando el tiempo de prolongación inicialmente establecido ya se había superado. El RC Deportivo considera que una prolongación de estas características, sin una justificación objetiva que explique semejante ampliación del tiempo anunciado, resulta inadmisible y compromete las garantías competitivas que deben regir cualquier encuentro profesional. Esta situación adquiere todavía mayor gravedad si se tiene en cuenta que se produce después de dos jornadas consecutivas en las que el Dépor ABANCA también se ha visto perjudicado por decisiones arbitrales. Son, por tanto, tres jornadas consecutivas en las que las actuaciones arbitrales han tenido consecuencias negativas para los intereses deportivos de nuestro equipo. El RC Deportivo es un firme defensor e impulsor del fútbol femenino. Nuestro compromiso con su crecimiento y profesionalización no se limita a las declaraciones, sino que se demuestra con hechos. Una de las expresiones más claras de esta apuesta es que el Dépor ABANCA disputa sus encuentros como local en ABANCA RIAZOR, el estadio del deportivismo, ofreciendo al fútbol femenino el espacio, la visibilidad y la dimensión que merece. En esta ocasión, más de 4.000 personas presenciaron en directo lo sucedido y fueron testigos del atropello sufrido por nuestro equipo. Una afición que acudió a apoyar al Dépor ABANCA y que merece, como nuestras futbolistas y nuestro club, el máximo respeto y unas condiciones de competición justas. El fútbol femenino merece el mismo nivel de profesionalidad, exigencia y garantías competitivas que cualquier otra competición. No puede construirse su crecimiento sin abordar con responsabilidad una cuestión tan determinante como la calidad del arbitraje, la coherencia de los criterios aplicados y la confianza de los clubes en el funcionamiento de la competición. Por todo ello, el RC Deportivo considera imprescindible que los organismos competentes analicen lo sucedido, ofrezcan las explicaciones oportunas y adopten las medidas necesarias para evitar que situaciones como esta vuelvan a repetirse. Nuestro compromiso con el fútbol femenino es firme e irrenunciable. Precisamente por ese compromiso, el RC Deportivo no va a permanecer en silencio ante actuaciones que perjudican a sus futbolistas, condicionan el desarrollo de la competición y dañan la credibilidad de una modalidad que necesita seguir creciendo con las máximas garantías".

articles.title: USC's latest terrible loss to Indiana Hoosiers might be the final straw for Lincoln Riley in LA
articles.summary: Jayden Maiava's red-zone interception and USC's five trips inside the Indiana 20 yielding just 13 points defined the crushing 27-13 collapse.
articles.body: Where have we ever seen this movie before? The USC Trojans, with their season and hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff on the line, on the road against another good team, needing to come through late in the fourth quarter to finally get the breakthrough win they need to reach the next level. And they came up short. While there's more to Saturday's 27-13 loss to the Indiana Hoosiers than any one play or incident, the embodiment of the Trojans' season, of head coach Lincoln Riley's tenure at USC, came halfway through the fourth quarter. INDIANA HOOSIERS BOOST COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF HOPES WITH 27-13 WIN OVER USC TROJANS Down 20-13, SC moved the ball down the field quickly, with Jayden Maiava completing a 34-yard pass to superstar freshman Trent Mosley to set up 1st-and-goal from the Hoosier's 8-yard-line. A quick two-yard run set up 2nd-and-goal from the six with 6:34 remaining. Maiava dropped back to pass and...telegraphed his intentions by staring down receiver Kayden Dixon-Wyatt, ignoring Indiana linebacker Isaiah Jones, and delivering a perfectly thrown and timed interception. Just like that, a potential tie game became Indiana ball. And just as they so often have, the Trojans defense couldn't get the ball back with the game still in reach. The Hoosiers went 93 yards on just seven plays, with a 42-yard touchdown pass from Grant Wilson to Charlie Becker effectively ending the game. Though it was officially ended when Maiava threw yet another interception on SC's final drive of the game. Again, to put the entire loss on that one play, 2nd-and-goal from the six, isn't doing SC's collapse enough justice. The Trojans dropped not one, not two, not three, but four interceptions. One thrown directly to a defense back that bounced off his chest. One that went through a defenders hands on a diving try in the end zone. One in which SC actually did catch the ball, miraculously, only to have it knocked away by the slightest bit of contact. And another just for fun. They missed two field goals, a 51-yard try that hit off the upright, and, somehow, a 27-yard attempt that wasn't even close. To make matters worse, a random Indiana fan nailed a field goal from almost that exact same spot a few minutes later. The missed attempt came after a 3rd-and-8 with an obvious pass interference on the Hoosiers incorrectly waved off because a linebacker got a fingertip the pass. Per NCAA rules, a tipped ball negates pass interference, but contact before the ball is touched should still be enforced. The contact on the play came before, and after, the tip, but the refs apparently determined otherwise. Though the fact it was even close points to Maiava's poor pass and decision making. LINCOLN RILEY HAS CONFRONTATION WITH OHIO STATE AD, READS PREPARED STATEMENT TO MEDIA AFTER HUGE USC WIN USC's two fourth quarter drives, pre-garbage time, resulted in 17 plays for 148 yards, both reaching to the Indiana 10-yard-line, and...zero points. Not three points, zero points. 148 yards on two drives, zero points. That wasn't an aberration; USC drove into the Indiana red zone five times throughout the game and scored just one touchdown. Five red zone opportunities, 13 total points. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE USC's defense was frequently in the right place at the right time, as evidenced by the four dropped interceptions, but they also gave up their share of trademark back-breaking mistakes too. With the game still tied late in the third quarter, Indiana had a 37-yard run, helped along by an obvious holding on No. 11 against a USC linebacker that wasn't called, that set the Hoosiers up for a go-ahead touchdown. After Maiava's pick, SC needed a stop to get the ball back. Instead, the Hoosiers went four-yard run, five-yard run, eight-yard run, 12-yard run, two-yard run, five-yard-run, 42-yard touchdown pass. That was the fourth play of 30+ yards the SC defense gave up to an offense run by a backup quarterback. It was a microcosm of the problems with the Lincoln Riley era in LA. Ten positives, outweighed by five negatives. A defense that isn't good to win games on their own. Missed opportunities on offense, particularly with short fields, missed field goals, and in the post Caleb Williams-era, quarterback play that simply isn't good enough. Especially on the road. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The loss was eerily reminiscent of the USC-Notre Dame game in 2025, when the Trojans took a 24-21 lead in the third quarter, then immediately gave up a 100-yard kickoff return. Still only down 27-24 after a missed PAT, Maiava threw yet another back breaking interception around midfield. The SC defense held, and the offense got the ball back, drove down to the Notre Dame 37-yard-line and...Makai Lemon fumbled on a trick play. The Irish scored on the ensuing drive, all but ending the game. Though Maiava added another late pick on the final drive of the game, just as he did against Indiana. Much of the blame for Saturday's loss can be placed on the players; dropped picks aren't Riley's fault, and Maiava's interception was a textbook case of poor quarterback vision. But at some point, the blame has to come back on Riley, doesn't it? This loss wouldn't have mattered as much if the Trojans had just beaten a very mediocre Wisconsin team on the road. They scored seven points and lost. Or if they'd have been able to hold serve against the Oregon Ducks playing backup QB Dylan Raiola for most of the game, at the LA Coliseum. They couldn't. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Maiava's played in a whopping 29 games for USC and Lincoln Riley now, and hasn't improved much. His footwork is awful, frequently unnecessarily throwing off his back foot. He often makes terrible decisions in pressure situations. His accuracy is atrocious as soon as there's pressure, and despite being a fairly mobile quarterback, he's all but stopped moving up in the pocket or running for free yards. That's a necessity in modern college football, and Maiava no longer even attempts it. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Some of that's on him, yes, but Riley's claim to fame is his work with quarterbacks. Why hasn't Maiava gotten better? Or why did he not evaluate Maiava's weaknesses and hit the transfer portal hard to find someone better? We're somehow just two weeks removed from SC fans storming the field after a huge win over Ohio State, but with the Trojans once again out of the College Football Playoff, once again suffering a disastrous, self-inflicted loss on the road, once again staring down the barrel of a long offseason of wondering what went wrong, it's once again enough to start the "Lincoln Riley hot seat" conversations. Particularly considering RIley's dismissive pre-written statement after the Buckeyes' win implying that he always knew the Trojans would peak at the right time and get into the tournament. Already, reports have suggested the Trojans could put his buyout together. And the crosstown rivalry game on Thanksgiving weekend might be the last try he has of staying in LA. UCLA in year one under Bob Chesney is a near-lock for the playoff, while Riley in year five is once again on the outside looking in. Lose to the Bruins, in a symbolic changing of the guard in LA, and it seems impossible that he's back at the Coliseum in 2027. It's a roller coaster, and most of the SC fanbase is ready for it to end.

articles.title: Lamine, a Anderson tras su penalti: “Tonto, tonto”
articles.standfirst: Tras robar a Quansah, Lamine forzó la roja de Anderson y lo apremió a abandonar el campo para lanzar cuanto antes el penalti de la remontada
articles.summary: Tras robar a Quansah, Lamine forzó la roja de Anderson y lo apremió a abandonar el campo para lanzar cuanto antes el penalti de la remontada
articles.body: Inglaterra llevaba camino de arrollar a España. Los de Thomas Tuchel, muy superiores en lo físico, mandaban 0-3 en el Metropolitano cuando apareció el momento que cambió el guion: una recuperación de Lamine Yamal sobre Quansah. El delantero del Barça robó el balón y se plantó prácticamente solo ante Trafford. Por detrás llegó Elliot Anderson, que lo agarró y lo derribó cuando encaraba la portería. El colegiado señaló penalti y mostró la tarjeta roja directa al centrocampista inglés, que dejaba a su equipo con diez. La acción tuvo continuación verbal. Nada más levantarse, Lamine se dirigió a Anderson y le repitió “tonto, tonto”, antes de apremiarle para que abandonara el césped cuanto antes. Desde el punto de penalti, Mikel Oyarzabal no falló y recortó distancias, un gol que devolvió a España a un partido que tenía cuesta arriba. La rendija que abrió Lamine con su robo y su penalti provocado reactivó a una selección que, hasta entonces, no había encontrado la manera de frenar el vendaval inglés.

articles.title: Zidane gana su primera 'final' con Francia... y podría cruzarse con España
articles.standfirst: Solventaron el choque contra Turquía y avanzan a cuartos de la Nations como líder de grupo
articles.summary: Solventaron el choque contra Turquía y avanzan a cuartos de la Nations como líder de grupo
articles.body: Zinédine Zidane afrontaba su primera 'final' como nuevo seleccionador de Francia tras la derrota sufrida en San Siro. Necesitaba, al menos, un punto para meterse en cuartos de la Nations. Las sensaciones volvieron a no ser las mejores. Pero hicieron los deberes ante Turquía y avanzaron como líderes de grupo. Podría cruzarse con España. La presencia de Mbappé, recuperado tras ausentarse contra Italia por molestias, acaparó todos los focos en una Francia donde Zidane, además de dar entrada a Konaté por la baja de Upamecano, renovó ambos laterales con la presencia de Kumbedi y Diouf. Yalçin, por su parte, ubicó a Özer bajo palos y plantó una línea de cinco atrás. Güler, libre por detrás de Gül, en una doble mediapunta junto a Uzun. El ambiente en Burdeos era descomunal. Había ganas de presenciar el retorno de 'Zizou', una de las grandes leyendas de un Girondins en horas extremadamente bajas. Sobre el césped, eso sí, rápido se despejó la incógnita sobre la posición de un Kylian Mbappé que, finalmente, se desempeñó como '9' y no en izquierda, donde su acostó Barcola. Francia, instalada en campo rival desde que se puso el balón en juego, trató de imprimirle dinamismo a sus circulaciones desde la movilidad en el centro del campo de Cherki, Da Cunha y un Rabiot que protagonizó las dos primeras ocasiones. La primera, con un disparo potente y lejano; la segunda inundando el área para cabecear un centro de Kumbedi. Mbappé, a pesar de arrancar como punta, tenía libertad total para aparecer por cualquier carril y despegarse del marcaje de los tres centrales. En el 14', probó por primera vez con un 'zapatazo' que Özer se quitó de encima y, cinco minutos después, puso a correr a un Bradley Barcola que no acertó a resolver mano a mano. Le estaba tocando sacrificarse más de lo habitual a un Arda Güler lejos de su zona de mayor influencia. Turquía estaba demasiado hundida... pero Francia se fue bajando diluyendo. No volvió a probar a Özer hasta otro mano a mano de Mbappé en el 34'. Respondió Yüksek apareciendo indetectable desde segunda línea, pero no pudo superar a Maignan. Se 'alocó' el encuentro antes de llegar al descanso. Özer se lució con una 'palomita' para repeler un disparo marca de la casa de Olise desde el 'piquito' del área... y Turquía se libró de encajar el 1-0 después de que Mbappé sentase al meta del Lille. El punta del Real Madrid, sin embargo, arrancó en fuera de juego a la hora de dibujarle el desmarque a Konaté. La victoria de Bélgica sobre Italia metía miedo a Francia, puesto que cualquier gol de Turquía les dejaba fuera. Maignan, además, acabó la primera parte con problemas y tuvo que dejar su sitió a un Restes que ya debutó en el anterior parón. La tranquilidad, sin embargo, llegó en el 49'. Rabiot peinó un córner servido por Cherki que Topçu se marcó en propia. Francia pasaba a ser líder... pero se llevó un bueno susto con el tanto anulado a Güler menos de cinco minutos después por un fuera de juego en el origen de Yüksek. Arda estaba entrando en calor y Zidane, llegada la hora de partido, metió piernas frescas con Camavinga y un Eli Junior Kroupi que duplicó le renta en la recta final. Llegó demasiado tarde el 2-1 de Bardakci en el descuento a centro de Güler desde el banderín.

articles.title: Oklahoma Beats Ole Miss After FAA Impact, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Chambliss, Mateer
articles.summary: The No. 19 Ole Miss Rebels suffered a 24-17 loss against the Oklahoma Sooners on Sunday. Coming off a disappointing loss to Georgia, Ole Miss needed a victory to keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive, but the Sooners got in the way.
articles.body:
The No. 19 Ole Miss Rebels suffered a 24-17 loss against the Oklahoma Sooners on Sunday. Coming off a disappointing loss to Georgia, Ole Miss needed a victory to keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive, but the Sooners got in the way.

The game was preceded by plenty of turbulence due to the FAA's decision to ground all flights on Friday.

The flight disruptions affected Ole Miss' travel plans for Saturday's game in Norman, and the Southeastern Conference announced on Saturday morning that the game would be delayed a full day. Ole Miss insisted they did everything possible to avoid postponing the game, but Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny slammed the decision and claimed it " isn't fair " to the Sooners.

The delay ultimately didn't prove to be unfair to the Sooners on the field as Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer notched his fourth consecutive game without a turnover.

Here's a look at the top performers from both teams in Sunday's matchup:

Oklahoma took an early lead and never let Ole Miss climb its way back into the game. The Rebels went three-and-out on their opening drive, and Mateer engineered a 13-play, 74-yard drive that culminated with an eight-yard rushing touchdown to give the Sooners a 7-0 lead.

The Rebels were forced to punt on their following drive, and the Sooners made them pay for it with a 75-yard touchdown on the return by wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III.

Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss led the Rebels on an 11-play, 75-yard scoring drive that ended with running back Joshua Dye punching in a 19-yard rushing touchdown. The scoring dried up for the rest of the quarter as both teams alternated punting on four consecutive drives before Oklahoma ran out the clock to end the half.

The Sooners attempted to limit possessions in the second half with long drives. Ole Miss had just one possession in the third quarter after the Sooners opened the half with a 12-play, 70-yard scoring drive that took over six minutes off the clock. Oklahoma's next drive took 14 plays and lasted nearly eight minutes, but ended with kicker Tate Sandell missing a 39-yard field goal attempt.

Chambliss connected with wide receiver Caleb Odom for a 26-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to cut Oklahoma's lead down to one score, but Sandell — who missed two kicks in the fourth quarter — extended the Sooners' lead with a 41-yard field goal.

Ole Miss kicked a field goal to cut the lead back down to one score again, and the Rebels made the game interesting by recovering an onside kick in the final minute. Ole Miss gained 26 yards in six plays, but time ultimately ran out and Chambliss' final heave into the end zone fell incomplete.

Oklahoma improved to 6-4 (4-3 SEC), while Ole Miss fell to 6-4 (4-4 SEC).

articles.title: Spain 2-3 England: Three Lions hold on for famous win after Elliot Anderson red card to top Nations League Group A3
articles.summary: Match report as England secure a stunning 3-2 win over Spain to end the world champions' 43-game unbeaten run and finish top of Nations League Group A3; Three Lions raced into a three-goal lead then clung on after Elliot Anderson's red card
articles.body:
Thomas Tuchel's side were sensational for an hour in Madrid, taking the lead when Harry Kane scored a penalty at the end of the first half and then adding quickfire goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But a one-sided game was turned on its head when Elliot Anderson was sent off for a last-man foul on Lamine Yamal following Jarell Quansah's error, allowing Mikel Oyarzabal to score from the spot.

Spain reduced the deficit to one goal when substitute Nico Williams converted Lamine Yamal's cross after Anthony Gordon had been dispossessed, but England clung on thanks to James Trafford.

The goalkeeper, selected ahead of Jordan Pickford, made a string of saves as Spain peppered the England goal, including a stunning double stop when he denied Fermin Lopez then somehow pushed Oyarzabal's follow-up around the post at full stretch.

His heroics, in addition to a vital last-man challenge by White on Williams, allowed the Three Lions to end Spain's 43-game unbeaten run with a historic victory which ensures they will be seeded in the Nations League quarter-final draw.

It appeared certain to be a more emphatic victory when White drilled the third goal through the legs of Unai Simon after Konsa had headed in Declan Rice's corner for the second. Spain had not even registered a shot on target at that point.

But Anderson's red card, after Quansah was caught on the ball by Lamine Yamal, reinvigorated Spain and meant England had to show the qualities demonstrated in their World Cup last-16 win over Mexico at the Azteca Stadium in July.

Their steel, and the contribution of their goalkeeper, got them over the line.

"We are fully aware of the performance we put out there for 60-65 minutes. To be 3-0 up and deservedly 3-0 up.

"Of course the red card and penalty changed the momentum and the characteristic of the game. Thirty minutes against Spain, in Spain, feels like three hours.

"That is the statement and significance of this victory: that it was deserved and the result followed the performance.

"It was on the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit and togetherness. It was on highest level football wise on all aspects of the game.

"That was an excellent performance. A wonderful feeling in the dressing room. Everyone was very tired. We overcame some difficult moments.

"We're aware what steps we took now after the World Cup. It's the best feeling."

Rice: We knew we were going to beat them

"We knew we could beat them. We knew we were going to beat them today.

"The message from the manager after the Croatia game was so positive. The message from the boys, everyone pushing together, knowing that we're going to come here and not sit back and hit them on the counter.

"We knew from the first minute - our first 10 minutes was probably the best we've played in a 10-minute spell. Pressure, pressure, pressure, we could have had two or three.

"The red card changes the course of the game as it could have been a couple more goals if I'm being honest."

84: TACKLE! White makes his crucial last-man tackle on Williams.

90+1: SAVES! Trafford rescues England again with a brilliant double save from Lopez and Oyarzabal.

England find out who they will face in the Nations League quarter-finals when the draw takes place on Friday November 20 at 11am.

The two-legged ties are scheduled for the March international break, with the first legs to be played between March 25 and 27 and the second legs between March 28 and 30.

articles.title: Ha nacido un nuevo clásico...
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Inglaterra - España
articles.body: El partido olía a trampa desde primera hora de la mañana. Inglaterra con ganas de revancha y España pensando en cerrar el año con una gran fiesta en el Metropolitano. Y la sensación de que algún día había que perder. Porque 43 partidos seguidos sin conocer la derrota son demasiados para cualquier equipo. Sea del deporte que sea. Pese a todo, España vendió muy cara la derrota. En una noche en la que fue claramente inferior a Inglaterra, estuvo a punto de lograr una remontada memorable. Se puso el partido muy cuesta arriba, con 0-3 en el marcador, y se rozó el empate. Faltaron cinco minutos y sobró Trafford, el portero inglés, que aguantó de pie el asedio final de España. La noche del Metropolitano deja la misma sensación que nos dejó la ida en Wembley: menos mal que la final del Mundial fue con Argentina... Porque con Inglaterra ahora mismo tenemos un buen hueso. Hay pique, nos tenemos ganas... España-Inglaterra: ha nacido un nuevo clásico. ¡Qué paradón a Laporte en el descuento! Una mano milagrosa para abortar la remontada de España, clasificar a Inglaterra como primera de grupo y acabar con la racha triunfal de La Roja, que se queda en 43 partidos. La mejor racha de la historia que se acaba en el último partido de un año inolvidable. Lamine volvió al once de España ante Inglaterra y lo hizo con el 10 a la espalda. Con Dani Olmo lesionado, el dorsal tenía dueño provisional: Víctor Muñoz, que lo había lucido ante la República Checa. Pero regresó Yamal y hubo intercambio. Aunque lo habitual es mantener los números durante los dos partidos de cada ventana, Lamine pidió el 10 y Víctor pasó al 19, reservado inicialmente para el azulgrana. Lamine tiene prisa por heredar el dorsal que le corresponde a Olmo por antigüedad. Presión para Dani… No falló Kane desde los once metros y tampoco Mikel. Oyarzabal alimentó la esperanza de remontada con un lanzamiento de penalti marca de la casa. Qué manera de lanzarlos, infalible. El delantero de España sumó su décimo gol en 2026 y vuelve a acabar el año como máximo goleador de La Roja. Igual que en 2024 y 2025. Se encendió la noche con la expulsión de Anderson y apareció Fermín en todo su esplendor. A pocos jugadores le sienta la efervescencia como al jugador del Barça, que empezó a aparecer por todos los lados del campo y a encender al Metropolitano con su entrega. Luego está su calidad con balón. Su pase a Lamine en la jugada del 2-3 fue una maravilla. El duelo fue principalmente desde el punto de penalti y se lo llevó Harry Kane. Fue al borde del descanso. Penalti de Cubarsí sobre el delantero inglés, que obviamente es el encargado de lanzarlo. El Balón de Oro contra el Guante de Oro. Ganó Kane, pero por poco. Acertó las intenciones de Harry el bueno de Unai Simón, pero el disparo seco del delantero fue inapelable. Gol y España obligada a remontar después de mucho tiempo. Tenía el partido controlado Inglaterra, con 0-3 en el marcador. Pero un error defensivo, una roja y todo saltó por los aires para Inglaterra. Rozó la remontada España y lo pasó fatal en el banquillo Tuchel, que revivió dos de los episodios del último Mundial: ante México, cuando se quedó con uno menos, y ante Argentina, cuando una remontada le dejó sin final. Sus cambios, pese a estar con 10, no ayudaron: quitó a Kane, Gordon y Bellingham de una tacada. Típico de Tuchel...

articles.title: Spain vs England player ratings: Jude Bellingham stars in Three Lions' victory
articles.summary: Spanish football reporter Elizabeth Conway and senior football correspondent Sami Mokbel give their player ratings for Spain v England.
articles.body:
England went 3-0 up before surviving a late onslaught after going down to 10 men to earn a landmark victory against World Cup holders Spain in Madrid on Sunday night.

Here's how we rated the players following the Three Lions' 3-2 victory and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Unai Simon: Made some brilliant saves early in the first half but still conceded three. 7

Marc Pubill: Had a bright 20 minutes against Anthony Gordon until he came off injured. 6

Pau Cubarsi: Gave away the penalty that Harry Kane scored for England's opener. 5

Aymeric Laporte: Always under pressure against Kane but came into the game more as the England striker dropped deeper after the sending off. 7

Marc Cucarella: Tried to get under Morgan Rogers' skin and kept him fairly quiet. 6

Martin Zubimendi: Made some decent challenges. 6

Fabian Ruiz: Made little impact in midfield before he came off at half-time. 5

Mikel Merino: The Arsenal midfielder was ineffective and quiet for the first half - and then taken off at half-time. 5

Lamine Yamal: Lewis Hall and Jarell Quansah has to double up to contain him. Moments of brilliance throughout. 8

Alex Baena: The Atletico Madrid forward made some decent runs into the box. 7

Mikel Oyarzabal: Scored Spain's penalty to make it 3-1. Relatively quiet other than that. 7

Pedro Porro (on 20, Pubill): Worked hard against Gordon. Had a great chance against James Trafford. 7

Dean Huijsen (on 46, Cubarsi): Struggled initially against Kane but coped better after Elliot Anderson was sent off. 6

Pedri (on 46, Fabien Ruiz): Constructive and rarely wasted a pass. 8

Fermin Lopez (on 46, Merino) Very good and linked up with Yamal well. 8

Nico Williams (on 71, Zubimendi) Made an immediate impact with a goal and constantly a threat. 8

Subs not used: Barrios, Garcia, Munoz, Pino, Raya, Roca, Torres

James Trafford : Had little to do until Quansah's error led to Oyarzabal's successful penalty but made crucial saves in closing stages to see England home. 8

Ben White : That is one way to silence the boo-boys! Marked his first international start since March 2022 with a brilliant all-round display and the eventual winner. 8

Ezri Konsa : Returned to the side after missing Croatia game through injury and proved just how important he has become. Colossal. 8

Jarell Quansah : Was having a good night until making the mistake that led to Spain's opener from the spot and Anderson's red card. 5

Lewis Hall : Growing in stature at international level. Excelled in the attacking third and battled well against Yamal. 8

Elliot Anderson : Utterly brilliant until being shown a red card in trying to clear up Quansah's mess. Desperately unlucky. 8

Declan Rice : Organised and drove the team forward - all while on an early yellow card. Delivered the corner for England's second. 8

Jude Bellingham : In his adopted city, the Real Madrid midfielder swaggered around like he owned the place. Oozed quality. 9

Morgan Rogers : A disciplined display from the Chelsea forward and still created Spain problems in forward areas. 8

Anthony Gordon : A nuisance for Spain in every area of the field but dalliance in possession led to host's second to set up anxious finish. 6

Harry Kane : Won and dispatched England's penalty and Spain could not live with his intelligence at times. Sacrificed following Anderson's red card. 7

Subs not used: Pickford, Steele, Hill, Alexander-Arnold, Gibbs-White, Jobe Bellingham, Eze, Ngumoha.

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: England stun Spain to end La Roja’s 43-game unbeaten run
articles.summary: Spain suffer first defeat since March 2024 after losing 3-2 to England in Madrid despite grandstand finish.
articles.body:
England held on with 10 men to record a stunning win over Spain in Madrid in one of the great UEFA Nations League games.

The visitors had seen their hosts parade their World Cup trophy on the pitch before the game, but raced into a 3-0 lead inside an hour, before being reduced to 10 men on 65 minutes and having to cling on in a dramatic finale to pip Spain to top spot in Group A3 on goal difference.

It was a record 10th straight away win for the Three Lions, and it inflicted the first defeat on La Roja since they went down 1-0 in a friendly against Colombia in London in March 2024. The 43-game run saw them crowned European and World Champions along the way.

England produced a stunning start and might have been ahead inside the opening minutes, but Unai Simon made a brilliant reaction save to claw away Jude Bellingham’s close-range effort.

The visitors were irresistible in the first half, pressing high and denying the hosts time and space to find their rhythm, and Spain were unable to register a shot on target in the opening 45 minutes.

England led 1-0 at the break after Harry Kane latched onto Elliot Anderson’s pass in behind and drew a foul from Pau Cubarsi in the box. Following a brief VAR review into Anderson’s challenge on Marc Cucurella in the build-up, Kane stepped up to convert the penalty.

He fired to the right of Unai Simon to register his 93rd Three Lions goal on his 127th appearance in the final seconds of the half.

The visitors doubled their lead eight minutes after the turnaround as Declan Rice’s curling corner was met by a powerful downward header from the unmarked Ezri Konsa, his Arsenal teammate.

The hosts were in disarray four minutes later, when some slick counterattacking saw Bellingham slot through into space on the right of the box for the on-rushing Ben White to drill a low shot past Simon at his near post.

The game changed 25 minutes from time when Jarell Quansah was dispossessed in his own half, and Anderson was shown a straight red card for denying a goalscoring opportunity by putting his arm on Lamine Yamal as he raced into the box.

After VAR confirmed the decision, Mikel Oyarzabal sent James Trafford – recalled in place of Jordan Pickford in goal – the wrong way to give the hosts hope.

They piled on the pressure and reduced the arrears further on the break on 75 minutes, when Yamal’s first-time cross from the right was swept in off the post by substitute Nico Williams.

La Roja laid siege to the England goal in the closing stages as they sought a goal to extend their unbeaten run and claim top spot in Group A3. But Trafford produced a stunning double save in stoppage time, diving to his right to parry a shot from Fermin Lopez, then somehow bouncing up to turn the follow-up from Aymeric Laporte around the upright.

England held on to secure first place in the group on goal difference after both sides finished on 15 points.

Both sides will find out their Nations League quarterfinal opponents next March when the draw takes place on Friday. England is set to face one of the three A-Group runners-up, other than Spain, while La Roja will face one of the other three group winners.

articles.title: Bengals reveal 2 new injury designations hours before Week 10 vs. Steelers
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals announced 2 new injury designations for their Week 10 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
Less than 10 hours before kickoff, the Cincinnati Bengals announced two new injury designations for their Week 10 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football.

At approximately 11:30 a.m. ET, the Bengals announced that starting right guard Dalton Risner and backup offensive tackle Myles Hinton were both questionable to play against the Steelers with illnesses.

Risner, who was drafted by the Denver Broncos in the second round of the 2019 NFL Draft before joining the Bengals in 2025, has played a big part in keeping Joe Burrow protected in 2026, appearing in eight games, with Pro Football Focus crediting him with three sacks allowed in their October 29 update.

If Risner can't suit up, expect Jacob Bayer or Jalen Rivers to slot in as the starting right guard for Sunday Night Football.

articles.title: Inglaterra se cobró el Mundial
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Inglaterra vino al Metropolitano a compensarse por el Mundial perdido en esa turbulenta semifinal ante Argentina, y lo consiguió con una hora de gran juego y media de fútbol temeroso, agrupada ante su portero Trafford que, con tanta protección y todo, tuvo que salvar el 2-3 con media docena de imponentes paradas. En la primera hora me pareció la mejor Inglaterra que he visto desde la de 1966 y por eso me sorprendió para mal que se convirtiera en un equipo tan medroso al verse 1-3 y con diez. Ahí le faltó al banquillo serenidad para hacer ver que con dos goles de ventaja y los jugadores que tenía (Bellingham estuvo cumbre), podía plantar cara para lo que restara. Pero el caso es que al final ganó, lo que equivale a decir que frenó la racha de invencibilidad de España. Alguna vez tenía que ser y que todos los males sean así: perder un partido cada 44. Y si bien es cierto que en el primer tiempo estuvo mal, incapaz de salir de la estudiadísima presión inglesa y con algunos jugadores, particularmente Zubimendi, incapaces de manejarse en el intensísimo hombre a hombre de los ingleses, el arreón final redimió todo lo anterior y mereció el premio del empate, que si no llegó fue por la noche inspirada de Trafford. Clasificados para cuartos de final ya estábamos, pero ahora tendremos que jugarlos contra un campeón de grupo y con el partido de vuelta fuera. Me sorprendió de salida que no estuvieran ni Pedri ni Fermín, el primero por la serenidad de su manejo, el segundo porque es un torbellino con precisión, inteligencia y gol. Quizá De la Fuente estaba preocupado por la estatura ante los córners, y trató de compensar la que faltaba con la ausencia de Rodri, que incluye entre sus tareas complementar a los centrales en los balones altos. Es curioso que a pesar de eso nos llegara el 0-3 en un cabezazo de Konsa en un córner, cabeceando solo y a placer. Perdimos, pero hay dos cosas que rescatar: la vergüenza torera del final y sobre todo Lamine Yamal, el único que en la primera parte consiguió aparecer, el que abrió la esperanza con la recuperación y el penalti que dieron el 1-3, y luego dio el pase que valió el 2-3 de Nico. Con ese superjugador, más Rodri cuando vuelva y el espíritu del tramo final, podemos mirar con optimismo lo que viene.
